objective.name: wrapper_ready
objective.description: Internal execution signal emitted by a wrapper when it becomes ready.

#root.role: Resolve the wrapper runtime from the wrapper origin context, mark it ready when appropriate, and release the readiness waiter.

effects.wrapper_runtime: The target wrapper runtime readiness flags and timestamps may be updated.

transformation_contract.morphing: An internal wrapper-ready signal becomes an updated ready state for the targeted wrapper runtime.
invariants: wrapper_ready is an internal one-way execution signal and does not emit a response payload.
The target wrapper is resolved from the originating wrapper transport context, not from params.
The ready transition only applies when the wrapper runtime is starting or running, not yet marked ready, and has no recorded readiness error.
success: When the signal is accepted, the wrapper runtime is marked ready, ReadyAt is stamped, and any readiness waiter is released.
A wrapper-ready trace event may be emitted when the readiness waiter is released.
failure: Signals from contexts that do not resolve to a known wrapper are ignored rather than producing an external error.
Missing execution frame or wrapper registry prevents state mutation and leaves the signal effectively as a no-op.
notes: This capability is reserved for internal wrapper lifecycle coordination inside Execution.
There are intentionally no declared outputs because callers should observe wrapper state indirectly rather than through a direct response.
